# Cost

**About $1.20 a month**, and almost all of it is monitoring. Generated by `python scripts/cost_model.py` from the assumptions at the top of that file: us-east-1 on-demand list prices as of October 2026, rounded up, free tier ignored (so this is what an account pays after its first year).

| Item | USD / month |
|---|---:|
| Lambda (4 functions, daily, arm64, cold-start init included) | 0.012 |
| Step Functions (standard, ~6 transitions a day) | 0.005 |
| S3 storage (~0.2 GB with old versions) + requests | 0.012 |
| Athena (300 queries, each under the 10 MB minimum) | 0.015 |
| Glue Data Catalog (6 tables) | 0.000 |
| CloudWatch custom metrics (2) | 0.600 |
| CloudWatch alarms (5) | 0.500 |
| CloudWatch Logs | 0.025 |
| ECR image storage | 0.035 |
| **Total** | **1.20** |

Reads from `s3://noaa-gsod-pds` cost me nothing: the AWS Open Data programme pays for that bucket's requests and egress, and the lake sits in the same region (ADR-007).

## What I did to keep it there

| Decision | Saving |
|---|---|
| **DuckDB in Lambda instead of a Glue Spark job** | ~$0.44/month, and a test suite that runs in 13 seconds instead of needing a Glue dev endpoint |
| **Partition projection instead of a daily Glue crawler** | ~$2.20/month, and no schema drift from a malformed file |
| **Step Functions instead of MWAA** | ~$358/month. For one four-step daily job, MWAA would be ~300x the rest of the bill |
| **Athena instead of Redshift Serverless** | ~$90/month at one hour of use a day; the gold tables are ~300 KB |
| **Daily file diff instead of a Kinesis stream** | ~$29/month for an always-on stream in front of a once-a-day file |
| **Only metrics that have an alarm** | Each custom metric is $0.30/month. I first emitted four; two had no alarm, so they now go to the logs, where Logs Insights can still query them. |
| **EMF log lines instead of `PutMetricData`** | No API calls and no extra permission; the metric comes out of a log line |
| **Parquet + zstd, partitioned by year** | A query filtered on one year reads ~30 KB instead of the whole table |
| **1 GB per-query scan cap on the Athena workgroup** | Caps a runaway query at half a cent |
| **Lifecycle rules** | Noncurrent raw versions expire after 90 days, silver/gold after 30, Athena results after 7, quarantine after 180 |
| **No Glacier or IA transitions** | Most objects are under the 128 KB minimum billable size for IA, so a transition would cost more than it saves |
| **arm64 (Graviton) Lambdas** | ~20% cheaper per GB-second |
| **Log retention 14-30 days** | CloudWatch keeps logs forever by default |
| **AWS Budget at $5** | An email at 80% and on a forecast overrun |

## Where the money would go at scale

- **More stations or hourly data.** Lambda and S3 stay pennies until data is in the tens of GB. The first real cost would be Athena scans if analysts query raw-grain hourly data without partition filters, which the workgroup cap limits.
- **More alarms.** Each alarm is $0.10 and each metric $0.30. Per-station metrics with a `station` dimension would be 15 billed metrics; I keep per-station detail in the `station_health` table instead.
- **SMS alerts.** International SMS to Nepal through SNS costs far more per message than a local Nepali gateway. At 1,000 subscribers and a dozen alert days a month, SMS would dwarf everything above; a local aggregator would be the choice.
